purpose_note: These original questions help explore work interests. They are not a clinical or validated psychometric assessment and do not determine a career outcome.

interest_questions.prompt: I enjoy setting up tools, systems, or equipment and seeing them work in practice.
When something technical breaks, I usually want to investigate and fix it myself.
I like turning a written plan into something concrete that others can use.
I enjoy working out why a system behaves the way it does.
I like finding patterns in complex information before making a decision.
I am comfortable experimenting, comparing evidence, and revising my first answer.
I notice when a digital experience feels confusing, awkward, or visually unbalanced.
I enjoy finding more elegant or imaginative ways to present an idea.
I care about how an interface, chart, or explanation makes people feel and understand.
I find it satisfying to help another person understand a difficult topic.
I prefer work where I can listen to different needs before choosing a solution.
I am energised by collaborating with people who have different strengths from mine.
I enjoy turning a vague problem into a clear plan that people can act on.
I am comfortable proposing an idea and persuading others to try it.
I am motivated by setting a goal, deciding priorities, and moving work forward.
I enjoy creating order in information so that it is easy to find and reuse.
I prefer clear processes when accuracy, security, or reliability matters.
I naturally check details before sharing work with other people.
